title: Retinoblastoma: Comprehensive Management Protocol
summary: Retinoblastoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy of childhood. This roadmap details the multi-modal approach to ocular salvage and life preservation, adhering to the latest International Classification for Retinoblastoma (ICRB) standards.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Retinoblastoma (Rb) arises from the malignant transformation of primitive retinal neuroectodermal cells. It is caused by biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumor suppressor gene (13q14). Hereditary cases (40%) involve germline mutations, predisposing to bilateral/multifocal disease and secondary cancers (e.g., osteosarcoma). Sporadic cases (60%) are typically unilateral and unifocal.

rows: Local subretinal fluid or isolated seeds
Diffuse subretinal fluid or massive/diffuse seeds
Neovascular glaucoma, hemorrhage, or tumor at lens

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Exam under anesthesia (EUA) with wide-field fundus imaging.
Step 2: B-scan ultrasonography (to assess calcification and extent).
Step 3: MRI Orbit/Brain (with/without contrast) to rule out trilateral Rb.
Step 4: Systemic staging (Bone marrow/CSF) for high-risk extraocular features.
Step 5: Genetic counseling and RB1 mutation analysis.

sections.title: Emergency Warning Signs
content: Rapid onset proptosis or orbital mass.
Any pupil asymmetry or fixed dilated pupil.
Family history of Rb (immediate screening required).

content.explanation: C: Chemotherapy (Systemic/IAC), C: Cryotherapy, C: Chemoreduction-Laser (TTT), P: Plaque radiotherapy.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Calcification is the hallmark of Rb on imaging (CT/USG).
Always screen the fellow eye; unilateral Rb in a child under 1 is highly suspicious for germline mutation.
Trilateral Rb: Bilateral ocular Rb + midline intracranial primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET).
Intra-arterial chemotherapy (IAC) is now the standard for eye salvage in groups B-D.
